facts.statement: Aegisuchus was named in 2012 by paleontologists Casey Holliday and Nicholas Gardner.
facts.quote: The type species Aegisuchus witmeri was named in 2012 by paleontologists Casey Holliday and Nicholas Gardner

facts.statement: The discoverers nicknamed Aegisuchus "Shieldcroc" because of its shield-like skull shape.
facts.quote: who nicknamed it "Shieldcroc" for the shield-like shape of its skull

facts.statement: Aegisuchus is an extinct genus of giant, flat-headed crocodyliform belonging to the family Aegyptosuchidae.
facts.quote: Aegisuchus is an extinct monospecific genus of giant, flat-headed crocodyliform within the family Aegyptosuchidae

facts.statement: Aegisuchus fossils were found in the Kem Kem Formation of southeast Morocco from the Cenomanian age of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: It was found in the Kem Kem Formation of southeast Morocco, which dates back to the Cenomanian age of the Late Cretaceous epoch

facts.statement: Aegisuchus has a unique circular, raised, and rough-surfaced boss on the center of its skull table.
facts.quote: At the center of the skull table is a raised and rough-surfaced boss on the parietal bone that is shaped like a circle

facts.statement: Aegisuchus possessed a rectangular projection on the quadrate bone that served as an attachment point for jaw-closing muscles.
facts.quote: The quadrate bone in the temporal region of the skull has a rectangular projection called the adductor tubercle, which served as an attachment for muscles that closed the jaw

facts.statement: Aegisuchus has the largest braincase volume of any known crocodyliform, measuring 40 cubic centimetres.
facts.quote: At 40 cubic centimetres, the braincase of Aegisuchus is much larger in volume than that of any other crocodyliform

facts.statement: Estimates based on skull proportions suggest Aegisuchus could have reached lengths between 15 and 22 meters.
facts.quote: A similar ratio between braincase and body length puts Aegisuchus at 15 to 21 m long when based on the proportions of long-snouted gharials, or 16 to 22 m long when based on the proportions of short-snouted crocodiles

facts.statement: Critiques of the original size estimates suggest Aegisuchus may have had a skull 62 to 90 cm long and a total length of about 3.9 meters.
facts.quote: A reader comment posted to the original description provided regression equations failed to replicate the reported skull length, suggesting actual skull length can be 62 to 90 cm long, and total length would be around 3.9 m

facts.statement: The unique vascular channels in Aegisuchus's skull may have functioned to thermoregulate blood flow to the brain and eyes.
facts.quote: Given that the blood vessel channels run into the braincase, the vascularized tissue may have served a thermoregulatory role by heating blood going to the brain and eyes

facts.statement: The central boss on Aegisuchus's skull may have served as an eyespot used in mating displays.
facts.quote: The central boss may have been used in mating displays, appearing as an eyespot

facts.statement: Aegisuchus likely hunted as an ambush predator by resting at the water's surface.
facts.quote: The flattened shape of the skull of Aegisuchus suggests that it was an ambush predator resting at the surface of the water

facts.statement: Aegisuchus likely had eyes positioned to face directly upward without surrounding raised ridges.
facts.quote: Aegisuchus probably had eyes that faced directly upward, with no raised ridges surrounding the sockets

facts.statement: Aegisuchus had a highly flexible connection between its skull and spine, allowing it to lift its head higher than other crocodilians.
facts.quote: Aegisuchus has a very flexible articulation between the skull and vertebral column, allowing a greater degree of skull elevation than other crocodilians

facts.statement: Aegisuchus shared its delta habitat with fishes, turtles, snakes, lizards, pterosaurs, and dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Aegisuchus lived within this delta alongside fishes, turtles, snakes and varanid lizards, pterosaurs, and sauropod and theropod dinosaurs

facts.statement: Aegisuchus likely preyed on coelacanths, lungfish, and bichirs found in its environment.
facts.quote: Possible prey include coelacanths, lungfish, and bichirs, all of which have been found in the Kem Kem beds

facts.statement: Aegisuchus may have been prey for larger predators like Spinosaurus.
facts.quote: Aegisuchus could have potentially fallen prey to much larger predators such as Spinosaurus

facts.statement: Aegisuchus belongs to the family Aegyptosuchidae, which also includes the genus Aegyptosuchus.
facts.quote: Aegisuchus is a member of the family Aegyptosuchidae, along with the genus Aegyptosuchus

facts.statement: Aegisuchus is known only from a partial neurocranium fossil cataloged as ROM 54530.
facts.quote: Aegisuchus es conocido únicamente a partir de un resto parcial del neurocráneo, que conserva la bóveda craneana y las regiones parietal y occipital, catalogado como ROM 54530.

facts.statement: A circular, rough-surfaced protuberance rises from the center of the flat top of the skull, surrounded by a shallow depression.
facts.quote: Sobre el hueso parietal, en el centro de la parte superior plana del cráneo, se erige una protuberancia circular de superficie rugosa, rodeada por una fosa somera.

facts.statement: A rectangular projection on the quadrate bone served as an attachment site for jaw-closing muscles.
facts.quote: El hueso cuadrado, en la región temporal del cráneo, tiene una proyección rectangular (tubérculo aductor), el cual servía como zona de inserción para los músculos que cerraban la mandíbula.

facts.statement: Capitate processes, bony projections on the laterosphenoid bones, protrude from the front of the skull on each side.
facts.quote: En el frente del cráneo sobresalen a cada lado los procesos capitados, unas proyecciones óseas sobre los huesos lateroesfenoides.

facts.statement: A bony rim or torus borders the lateral edge of each dorsal temporal fenestra on the frontal surface.
facts.quote: Sobre la superficie frontal se presenta un borde óseo o torus en el margen lateral de cada fenestra.

facts.statement: The back of the skull is wide with large projections on the exoccipital bones that likely supported large epaxial muscles in the upper neck.
facts.quote: La parte posterior del cráneo es ancha, con grandes proyecciones sobre los huesos exoccipitales que pudieron haber sostenido grandes músculos epaxiales en la parte superior del cuello.

facts.statement: The Aegisuchus neurocranium has a volume of 40 cubic centimeters, which is larger than that of any other crocodiliform.
facts.quote: El neurocráneo de Aegisuchus, de 40 centímetros cúbicos, posee un volumen mucho mayor que el de cualquier otro crocodiliforme.

facts.statement: Based on neurocranium proportions, the total skull length of Aegisuchus is estimated to be between 2.08 and 2.86 meters.
facts.quote: Basándose en la proporción del neurocráneo sobre la longitud total del cráneo en otros crocodilianos, se estima que la longitud total del cráneo de Aegisuchus pudo ser entre 2.08 a 2.86 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Body length estimates for Aegisuchus range from 15 to 21 meters based on gharial proportions, or 16 to 22 meters based on short-snouted crocodile proportions.
facts.quote: Una proporción similar entre el neurocráneo y la longitud corporal sitúa a Aegisuchus en el rango de 15 a 21 metros de largo basándose en las proporciones de los gaviales de hocico alargado, o 16 a 22 metros de largo si las proporciones se basan en cocodrilos de hocicos más cortos.

facts.statement: While it likely did not reach the maximum estimated lengths, Aegisuchus could have been longer than the largest known crocodiliforms like Deinosuchus and Sarcosuchus.
facts.quote: Aegisuchus casi con certeza no alcanzaba las máximas longitudes, pero podría ser mucho más largo que los mayores crocodiliformes, incluyendo a Deinosuchus, Gryposuchus, Purussaurus y Sarcosuchus.

facts.statement: As a "duck-billed" crocodiliform, Aegisuchus likely had a snout much longer relative to its body length than modern crocodilians.
facts.quote: Siendo un crocodiliforme "rostro de pato", Aegisuchus puede haber tenido un hocico mucho más largo con respecto a su longitud corporal que los crocodilianos actuales.

facts.statement: Deep parallel channels surrounding the central protuberance housed blood vessels, suggesting this area was covered by thick, complex skin.
facts.quote: Rodeando la protuberancia, la zona con superficie más suave tenía varios canales paralelos profundos para alojar los vasos sanguíneos, lo que sugiere que esta parte estaba cubierta por una piel gruesa y compleja.

facts.statement: This specific vascularization pattern has not been seen in any other crocodilian and may be unique to Aegisuchus.
facts.quote: Esta vascularización no ha sido vista en ningún otro crocodiliano, y puede haber sido única de Aegisuchus.

facts.statement: The vascularized tissue likely functioned in thermoregulation by warming blood flowing to the brain and eyes.
facts.quote: Dado que los canales de los vasos sanguíneos se dirigían al neurocráneo, el tejido vascularizado pudo haber tenido una función de termorregulación al calentar la sangre que iba hacia el cerebro y los ojos.

facts.statement: The central protuberance may have served as a display organ during mating, mimicking an eye spot.
facts.quote: La protuberancia central puede haber servido como órgano de despliegue durante el apareamiento, simulando ser un ocelo.

facts.statement: The postorbital bar, typically vertical in many crocodilians, is oriented almost horizontally in Aegisuchus.
facts.quote: La barra postorbital, un puntal óseo que suele estar orientado de forma vertical en muchos crocodilianos, se presenta en Aegisuchus casi horizontal.

facts.statement: The external medial adductor mandibulae muscle was larger and more important for jaw closure than in most crocodilians.
facts.quote: Músculos como el aductor mandibular externo medial, adquirió más importancia para la función de cerrar la mandíbula y su tamaño es mayor que el de la mayoría de los crocodilianos.

facts.statement: A depressed region in the lower posterior skull suggests large adductor muscles that facilitated opening the mouth.
facts.quote: Una región deprimida en la parte baja de la zona posterior del cráneo sugieren que sus músculos aductores eran también grandes, facilitando la abertura de la boca.

facts.statement: Aegisuchus had a very flexible joint between the skull and spine, allowing a greater angle of elevation than other crocodilians.
facts.quote: Aegisuchus tenía una articulación muy flexible entre el cráneo y la columna vertebral, permitiéndole un mayor ángulo de elevación que en otros crocodilianos.

facts.statement: During the Late Cretaceous, North Africa was a humid region near the Tethys Sea, connecting Gondwana and Laurasia.
facts.quote: Durante el Cretácico Superior, el norte de África era una región húmeda cercana al mar de Tetis, una vía marítima entre los continentes australes de Gondwana y las masas terrestres boreales de Laurasia.

facts.statement: Aegisuchus lived in the freshwater delta system of the Kem Kem Formation in Morocco.
facts.quote: En esta época, los sedimentos de la Formación Kem Kem de Marruecos fueron depositados en un sistema de delta de agua dulce.

facts.statement: Aegisuchus shared its habitat with fish, turtles, snakes, monitor lizards, pterosaurs, and sauropod and theropod dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Aegisuchus vivió en este delta junto a peces, tortugas, serpientes y lagartos varánidos, pterosaurios y dinosaurios saurópodos y terópodos.

facts.statement: With its flattened skull, Aegisuchus was likely an ambush predator.
facts.quote: Con su cráneo aplanado, Aegisuchus era probablemente un depredador de emboscada.

facts.statement: Possible prey included coelacanths, lungfish, and bichirs, all of which have been found as fossils in Kem Kem layers.
facts.quote: Sus posibles presas incluían celacantos, peces pulmonados y bichires, de todos los cuales han sido hallados fósiles en las capas de Kem Kem.

facts.statement: As an opportunistic predator, Aegisuchus may have also preyed on terrestrial vertebrates.
facts.quote: Como un depredador oportunista, Aegisuchus pudo haber depredado también vertebrados terrestres.

facts.statement: Aegyptosuchids represent a highly specialized and endemic branch of crocodiliforms during a time of increasing crocodilian diversity and geographic distribution.
facts.quote: Los egiptosúquidos representan una rama altamente especializada y endémica de crocodiliformes en una época en la que la diversidad y la distribución geográfica de los crocodilianos estaban aumentando.

facts.statement: The presence of Aegyptosuchids like Aegisuchus in North Africa suggests the initial evolution of crocodilians was centered around the Tethys Sea basin.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, la presencia de egiptosúquidos como Aegisuchus en el norte de África sugiere que la evolución inicial de los crocodilianos estuvo centrada alrededor de la cuenca del mar de Tetis.

facts.statement: Aegisuchus belongs to the parent group Aegyptosuchidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Aegyptosuchidae

facts.statement: Aegisuchus is classified in the family Aegyptosuchidae.
facts.quote: Family: Aegyptosuchidae

facts.statement: Aegisuchus is classified as a reptile.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Aegisuchus is Aegisuchus witmeri.
facts.quote: Type species: Aegisuchus witmeri

facts.statement: Aegisuchus lived from 100.5 to 93.9 million years ago during the Cenomanian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Cenomanian (100.5 to 93.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: It is debated whether the central protuberance served as a mating display organ mimicking an eye spot.
facts.quote: La protuberancia central puede haber servido como órgano de despliegue durante el apareamiento, simulando ser un ocelo.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest this vascularization may have been unique to Aegisuchus, though it has not been seen in any other crocodilian.
facts.quote: Esta vascularización no ha sido vista en ningún otro crocodiliano, y puede haber sido única de Aegisuchus.

facts.statement: Researchers infer that Aegisuchus likely had eyes directed straight up without elevated orbital rims, though this is based on comparisons with close relatives.
facts.quote: Aegisuchus probablemente tenía ojos dirigidos directamente hacia arriba, sin elevados bordes alrededor de las cuencas oculares.
